extraction_scope: Worker-6 final adjudication of mechanism claims from paper XML/PDF locators; no figure-derived numeric quantification was invented.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PG-1 and analogs in this paper
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper frames PG-1 as a beta-hairpin pore-forming antimicrobial peptide and tests membrane permeabilization with ONPG; PG-1 shows strong permeabilization near MIC while [V16R] has limited ONPG permeation at its MIC.
direct_assay_types: ONPG E. coli ML35p membrane permeability assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure 3 is qualitative/kinetic in the local evidence surface; exact curve values were not extracted as table values.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD and FTIR data support beta-hairpin/beta-structure context and indicate that [V16R] in DPC is more consistent with a dimer-like state while PG-1 supports denser oligomeric packing.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports oligomerization/structure interpretation, not a complete cell-level killing mechanism for every analog.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports in vivo mouse septicemia efficacy for [V16R] as preliminary therapeutic evidence, but this is efficacy evidence rather than a direct antimicrobial mechanism assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct in vivo target mechanism is established; dose optimization remains proposed by the authors.
